issues.description: The Bitmap24::set method's parameter order/names in the header do not match the implementation. In Bitmap24.hpp the declaration lists parameters as (int i_x, int i_y, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b) suggesting (x, y) order, while Bitmap24.cpp defines Bitmap24::set(int i_y, int i_x, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b) and uses the first parameter as the row (y) and the second as the column (x). This mismatch between declaration and definition (and the misleading parameter names in the header) can confuse students about the intended argument order when calling set(), even though the types are the same.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the declaration and definition parameter names and intended ordering consistent. Either change Bitmap24.hpp to declare set(int i_y, int i_x, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b) or change Bitmap24.cpp to define set(int i_x, int i_y, ...) and adjust the indexing accordingly. Also update the header documentation/comment to clearly state the expected argument order (row, column or x, y) to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The Bitmap24::set() parameter identifiers are inconsistent between the template and solution artifacts (and within the template). In the template repository header (Bitmap24.hpp) the parameters are declared as (int i_x, int i_y, ...), while the template implementation (Bitmap24.cpp) defines the function with parameters named (int i_y, int i_x, ...). The solution repository consistently uses (int i_y, int i_x, ...) in both header and implementation. This naming/order mismatch in the template header creates conceptual confusion for students about the intended argument order (x vs. y) and forces them to reconcile differing parameter names across declaration and definition as well as between template and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter names and their apparent order consistent across declaration and definition in the template to match the solution: change the template header signature to use (int i_y, int i_x, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b) so it aligns with the implementation and the solution, or alternatively adjust the implementation to match a clear header (preferably use (int i_y, int i_x) to reflect row/column ordering used in calls).
